_about: Zacharias Ursinus (1534-1583), chief author of the Heidelberg Catechism. The target is his Commentary on the Heidelberg Catechism, translated from the Latin by G. W. Williard, second American edition (Columbus: Scott & Bascom, 1852), Internet Archive OCR, raw; title page read. Williard is named on the title page and checked as translator.

ursinus-commentary: The Commentary of Dr. Zacharias Ursinus on the Heidelberg Catechism, tr. G. W. Williard, 2nd American ed. (Columbus, 1852)

_alternates.commentaryofzach00ursiuoft: Fourth American edition (Cincinnati, 1888), Toronto: a later printing of the same translation.
_alternates.commentaryofdrza00ursi: Princeton 'Third American Edition' (Cincinnati; the record's 1851 date is doubtful).

_pending.The Summe of Christian Religion, tr. Hen: The earlier English translation; only EEBO-type scans seen so far.
_pending.Heidelberg Catechism text (1563; Schaff,: A confession, not Ursinus's own book; belongs on a creeds shelf.

_excluded.ccel ursinus/catechism, ursinus/gospel: Short CCEL essays with no source and no rights line; their text appears to come from the Williard commentary, which is held.
_excluded.ccel ursinus/heidelberg, heidelberg1: The Catechism itself, served as a work-info page without text.
